label: heart-s6
summary: The model predicts heart disease from a linear score of the direct edges plus one small gated correction by sex and exercise angina, through a sigmoid. Its training AUC is 0.946. The direct score carries most of the discrimination: holding it at its training mean drops the AUC to 0.596; its largest weights per sd are the number of coloured vessels (ca, 1.57), asymptomatic chest pain (1.30) and a flat ST segment (1.04). The gate (units 1213 and 47) lowers the score for women without exercise angina (-1.76 logit on average over those 64 training women) and raises it for the 57 men without exercise angina whose unit 1213 stays off (0.81 on average). Exercise angina reaches the prediction through this gate alone (it has no direct edge, and the root has 0 direct edges of its own), and for such men the model gives a lower predicted risk with exercise angina than without it: 19% against 33% for the typical man, the reverse of the observed outcome rates (heart disease in 32% of those 57 men against 76% of the 63 men with exercise angina). Switching the gate off lowers the AUC to 0.925. A third part, an always-on unit on the upsloping ST indicator, is negligible (AUC 0.9454 without it). Resting blood pressure, maximum heart rate and the resting ECG have no edge into the network (in the typical case the predicted risk is 0.3334 at a maximum heart rate of 90 beats per minute and 0.3334 at 200 beats per minute).

resisted: No part resisted explanation. The slope offset (unit 3660) is described rather than explained: a near-negligible linear term routed through a unit that stays on for 242 of the 242 training rows. Why the gate makes exercise angina lower the predicted risk for men whose unit 1213 stays off is not explained by the structure; it may be offset by correlated inputs such as asymptomatic chest pain in the direct score, which was not tested here.
